clinician.final_diagnosis: A tension pneumothorax, possibly secondary to underlying COVID-19, was diagnosed.
clinician.trajectory_summary: The patient presented with acute respiratory distress, hypoxemia, and clinical signs suggestive of a left-sided pneumothorax. A chest X-ray confirmed a large left-sided tension pneumothorax with mediastinal shift and radiological signs of tension. Immediate emergency needle decompression was performed, followed by the insertion of a 12-French Seldinger chest drain, leading to immediate improvement in respiratory and cardiovascular physiology and lung re-expansion. Although an initial COVID-19 swab was negative, the infectious diseases team suspected underlying COVID-19 based on the patient's history and imaging, attributing the negative result to delayed presentation. Routine lab findings also indicated inflammation and possible superimposed bacterial infection on a background of COVID-19.

Immediate emergency needle decompression of the pneumothorax was performed.
A 12-French Seldinger chest drain was inserted following initial decompression.
